ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the left figure is a plan view, the solid lines indicate terrain contour lines, the dashed lines indicate phreatic surface contour lines, there is a river passing diagonally through the figure, a flow-direction arrow is marked beside the river, and MN is the position of the river cross section; the figure also marks the 40° latitude line and the 10° longitude line. The right side is the distribution map of equal-velocity lines in the MN river section, with M on the left and N on the right, and the equal-velocity lines and the deeper river channel are obviously biased toward the N bank side. Then reason: from the river flow direction in the left figure and the positions of the two banks at MN, it can be known that the N bank is the left bank in the downstream direction. The right figure shows that the left bank has a large flow velocity and strong erosion, indicating that the water flow is deflected to the left by the geostrophic deflection force, so this place is located in the Southern Hemisphere, and 40° in the figure should be understood as 40°S. Combining the relationship between the phreatic surface contour lines and the river in the left figure, it can be judged that the season shown in the figure is the local summer, that is, the Southern Hemisphere summer, roughly around December. The El Niño phenomenon often develops or appears significantly around Christmas and during the Southern Hemisphere summer, so the climatic anomaly that may occur at this time is the El Niño phenomenon.
